title: Document segmentation — Passage-Level Retrieval
description:
Passage-level retrieval treats long documents as addressable sections and returns only the passages that answer the question, with enough surrounding signal to stay honest. It is the foundation of grounded question answering: instead of handing an AI a whole book and hoping it cites correctly, the system retrieves the exact paragraphs, each stamped with document, section, and offsets. Core machinery includes passage segmentation, passage scoring, and offset-stable citations.

This record documents the document segmentation approach: Split documents into overlapping passages (sentences or paragraphs) so no claim is ever cut in half at a boundary.

Teaching ladder rank 1 (foundations): this record explains the core idea in plain terms — what inputs the tool takes, what outputs it produces, and when it is the right choice for an archive task.

# Passage-Level Retrieval demo: segment, score with BM25-lite, cite with offsets.
import math, re
DOC="""# Solar Sails
Sails catch photons. A large reflective sail can push a probe.
## Materials
Mylar is cheap but tears. Kapton survives heat better.
## Propulsion
Photon pressure is tiny but constant. Over months it adds up."""
def passages(doc):
    out=[]; pos=0
    for p in re.split(r"\n\n+",doc):
        p=p.strip()
        if p: out.append({"text":p,"start":doc.index(p,pos)}); pos=doc.index(p,pos)+len(p)
    return out
def score(q,p):
    qt=q.lower().split(); pt=p["text"].lower()
    return sum(pt.count(t)*(1.0/(1+pt.count(t))) for t in qt)
q="which material survives heat"
ranked=sorted(passages(DOC),key=lambda p:-score(q,p))
for p in ranked[:2]:
    print("score=%.3f offset=%d text=%r"%(score(q,p),p["start"],p["text"][:60]))

title: Streaming passage delivery — Passage-Level Retrieval
description:
Passage-level retrieval treats long documents as addressable sections and returns only the passages that answer the question, with enough surrounding signal to stay honest. It is the foundation of grounded question answering: instead of handing an AI a whole book and hoping it cites correctly, the system retrieves the exact paragraphs, each stamped with document, section, and offsets. Core machinery includes passage segmentation, passage scoring, and offset-stable citations.

This record documents the streaming passage delivery approach: Stream passages as they score above threshold instead of waiting for the full ranking to complete.

Teaching ladder rank 3 (advanced): this record covers production concerns — scaling behavior, failure modes, measurement, and the operational discipline needed to run this tool across a near-boundless archive.

Every record in this database is the full fully-formed file with all data — never a stub or description alone. This database holds 15 of the 1,000,000 target — the march to a million is in progress.
demo:
# Passage-Level Retrieval demo: segment, score with BM25-lite, cite with offsets.
import math, re
DOC="""# Solar Sails
Sails catch photons. A large reflective sail can push a probe.
## Materials
Mylar is cheap but tears. Kapton survives heat better.
## Propulsion
Photon pressure is tiny but constant. Over months it adds up."""
def passages(doc):
    out=[]; pos=0
    for p in re.split(r"\n\n+",doc):
        p=p.strip()
        if p: out.append({"text":p,"start":doc.index(p,pos)}); pos=doc.index(p,pos)+len(p)
    return out
def score(q,p):
    qt=q.lower().split(); pt=p["text"].lower()
    return sum(pt.count(t)*(1.0/(1+pt.count(t))) for t in qt)
q="which material survives heat"
ranked=sorted(passages(DOC),key=lambda p:-score(q,p))
for p in ranked[:2]:
    print("score=%.3f offset=%d text=%r"%(score(q,p),p["start"],p["text"][:60]))
